message.content:
Here’s a quick‑reference guide you can keep handy (or print out) so your piano stays happy and healthy:

| # | Tip | Why it matters |
|---|-----|----------------|
| **1** | **Control Humidity & Temperature** | Pianos expand/contract with moisture changes. Aim for ~45–55 % relative humidity and keep the room between 65–75°F (18–24°C). Use a hygrometer + humidifier/dehumidifier as needed. |
| **2** | **Regular Tuning** | Most pianos should be tuned at least twice a year (quarterly if you play often). A skilled tuner will adjust each note’s pitch and balance the overall sound. |
| **3** | **Professional Servicing** | Every few years bring the piano in for a full service—cleaning inside/outside, checking action parts, lubricating hammers, inspecting strings, and tightening bolts. |
| **4** | **Keep It Clean** | Wipe down keys, lid, pedals, and outer surfaces weekly with a soft microfiber cloth. Avoid harsh chemicals – a mild soap solution works fine. |
| **5** | **Use a Piano Cover When Not In Use** | Protects from dust, light damage, and accidental knocks. Make sure the cover fits snugly but doesn’t trap heat. |
| **6** | **Avoid Extreme Conditions** | Don’t leave the piano near radiators, heaters, air vents, or direct sunlight. Sudden temperature swings cause warping or cracking. |
| **7** | **Mind Your Footwear** | Shoes on the floor can scratch lacquered wood. Consider using slippers or placing a rug under the piano. |
| **8** | **Check the Pedals Regularly** | Loose pedal springs or worn pads reduce responsiveness. Tighten screws gently or replace worn components when necessary. |
| **9** | **Watch Out for Water Damage** | Even small spills can ruin internal mechanisms. If water gets onto the keyboard area, dry immediately and let the interior ventilate before playing again. |
| **10** | **Limit Heavy Impact** | Keep pets, children, or heavy objects away from the piano. Dropping something on the case can crack the frame or shift the bridge alignment. |
| **11** | **Monitor Soundboard Health** | Listen for new cracks or “dead” spots after tuning. These may indicate structural issues requiring a luthier’s attention. |
| **12** | **Record Maintenance History** | Maintain a logbook noting dates of tunings, repairs, and environmental readings. This helps spot trends and informs future care decisions. |

### Quick Checklist for Daily Care
- [ ] Dust keytops lightly once a week  
- [ ] Inspect for visible cracks or loose hardware daily  
- [ ] Adjust humidity controls nightly if needed  

By following these steps consistently, you'll preserve both the tonal quality and physical integrity of your piano for decades—and enjoy more reliable performance whenever you sit down to play!
